page: Microsoft Azure F4ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Fadsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 472 GB local disk and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3757.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2840.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded operations such as gzip compression at 40.89 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.86 GB/sec also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance metrics, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 14992.48 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8893.0, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only large block bandwidth at 53.01 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 34.32 GB/sec.

The instance exhibits a performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core workloads. While single-core execution is highly efficient, multi-threaded scaling and memory bandwidth remain average. For language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 340.4 tokens/sec on small 135M models, but prompt processing on medium 7B models drops to a weak 30.43 tokens/sec. Qualitatively, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and integrated 472 GB local storage offer balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. This profile is suitable for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text processing tasks that benefit from high clock speeds but do not require massive parallelization or GPU acceleration.
